Geometry: Naturally aspirated stacked-plate / louvered shield (Stevenson-screen type)
Description: Horizontal plates or louvers around the sensing element; passive crossflow
Water protection: Moderate (rain shielded by overlap; splash possible)
Thermal coupling to electronics: Low if sensor isolated from logger
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Vent open-area ratio; plate spacing; plate count; shield diameter; height AGL
Used in literature: Theisen 2020 (3D-PAWS naturally aspirated shield at 1.5 m)
Notes / source: Theisen: temp RMSE fell from 1.22 to ~1.08 C as wind rose -> ventilation-limited radiation error; key accuracy driver

Description: Nested truncated cones separated by spacers; sensor held inside an interior cone
Radiation blocking: Good (sensor shielded from direct light in 2nd cone)
Water protection: Good (20 mm spacers keep interior dry)
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Cone spacing (20 mm in Botero); number of cones; separator length; inlet area
Used in literature: Botero 2022 (PLA and ASA versions; SHT10 sensor; 20 mm M3 separators; 1-inch PVC coupling base)
Notes / source: Botero compared exposed vs PLA vs ASA shield vs Vantage Pro reference; modular and customizable; prints fine on open FDM in PETG

Description: Shield with a small fan forcing airflow over the sensor
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Fan flow rate (m3/h or m/s at sensor); power draw (W)
Used in literature: Suggested by Theisen 2020 (5 V fan to improve T/RH) - not implemented
Notes / source: Directly attacks ventilation-limited error; costs power -> accuracy vs autonomy tradeoff; adds a failure point

Geometry: Two-zone: sealed electronics box + external sensing region/probe
Description: Sealed compartment for logger/power; separate ventilated region or probe for ambient sensors
Water protection: High for electronics; sensor region separate
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Electronics-to-sensor separation distance; box IP rating; sensor-region open-area
Used in literature: Theisen 2020 (electrical junction box housed the Raspberry Pi; secondary sensor logged internal box temp)
Notes / source: Isolates self-heating from ambient measurement; pairs naturally with COTS box + printed shield on open FDM

Description: Single enclosure with vents or perforations; sensor shares volume with electronics
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Vent area ratio; internal free volume; distance sensor-to-PCB
Notes / source: Simple but couples electronics heat into the ambient reading; expect warm bias; keep as negative control

Description: Off-the-shelf sealed box (e.g., PVC/ABS) with cable glands
Thermal coupling to electronics: High if sensor inside; use as electronics zone only
Quantifiable proxy parameters: IP rating (IEC 60529); gland count; internal volume
Used in literature: Theisen 2020 (junction box used for the Pi)
Notes / source: Best for the sealed electronics zone; unsuitable to house ambient T/RH sensor due to heat/airflow

Description: Multiple stacked louver layers approaching meteorological-standard screen geometry
Manufacturability: More parts / longer print but all open-FDM friendly in PETG
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Louver count; louver angle; inter-louver gap; total open-area ratio
Notes / source: Higher passive performance than single-layer shield; tests how far passive design can close the gap before needing a fan

Description: Vertical chimney or helical path that promotes stack-effect airflow without a fan
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Stack height; flue cross-section; inlet/outlet area ratio; helix pitch
Notes / source: Aims for fan-like ventilation without power cost; effectiveness depends on temperature gradient and wind

Geometry: COTS junction box + replaceable vent/inlet module
Description: Off-the-shelf IP-rated electronics box plus a printed, swappable PETG vent or radiation-shield module for the sensor
Airflow mechanism: Passive through printed module (or fan option)
Water protection: High (COTS box) + module-dependent for sensor region
Thermal coupling to electronics: Designed-low (sensor in module, electronics in sealed box)
Manufacturability: Best open-FDM fit: buy the sealed box, print only the small module
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Module open-area; module material/finish; box IP rating; gland count
Used in literature: Hybrid of Theisen junction box + printed shield
Lab candidate (this study): YES - selected to test (strongest fit for open-FDM lab)
Notes / source: Decouples the hard sealing problem (buy it) from the printable shield problem; modules are cheap to iterate and field-replace

Description: Overlapping plates made from reflective insulation or folded white corrugated sheet
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Plate count; overlap; gap; albedo; open-area ratio
Used in literature: Tarara and Hoheisel 2007; Holden et al. 2013
Notes / source: Direct literature evidence that stacked plates outperform open/weakly perforated tubes

Description: 90-degree inlet elbow with concentric air-gap walls, insect screen, central sensor supports, and angled fan diffuser
Airflow mechanism: Forced convection (~0.5 m/s reported centerline velocity)
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Fan power; flow speed; elbow angle; air gap; sensor position
Notes / source: Direct accuracy-autonomy tradeoff; 680 mW fan and durability concerns

Description: Silver-coated square plates, black inner surfaces, annular layers, diversion pipe, eight vents, and cone reflector
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Vent count/area; coating reflectance; plate spacing; reflector angle
Notes / source: Explicitly addresses direct, reflected, and upwelling radiation

Description: Upper/lower square plates with symmetric curved bowl-cover shrouds around central probe
Quantifiable proxy parameters: Shroud spacing (30 mm reported); plate size; cavity velocity; material conductivity
Notes / source: Recent CFD and outdoor validation; manufacturability and weathering still need study
